Public static demo: synthetic data only. No AlarmX server, device access or interaction-log upload. Do not enter private data.

Create a visual query

Follow the controls, one step at a time. 21 task recipes and 59 screenshots demonstrate the S07.1 Query Design editor with its 32 synthetic rows.

Start with S07.1 in another tab, then choose a task from the contents. Each recipe starts from Reset query, except those explicitly marked as continuing the previous query. Search this page with Ctrl+F / Cmd+F.

Amber outlines are guide annotations identifying the relevant controls. Screenshots show real rendered GUI states, captured at 1440px desktop and 390px phone width. Your theme, zoom or toolbar overflow may change their positions. S07 remains a separate demo. This guide covers local single-table query design; all examples use synthetic data.

1. Start and apply a query

Open S07.1. Each recipe below starts with Reset query unless it says to continue. The initial design already contains Region, Qty, UnitPrice and Enabled.

  1. Locate the source and design grid

    The source card lists available fields. The grid below it describes the query: Field, Table, Sort, Show and Criteria. The top selector strip selects whole columns; the Field row edits their contents.

  2. Apply the current design

    Scroll below the query editor and click Apply query. The status reports 32 of 32 synthetic source rows and 32 result rows. Editing the design leaves the previous result visible until you apply again.

Back to contents

2. Add a column, choose its source and rename it

A field can appear more than once in the design. Adding a query column does not add a field to the source data.

  1. Click a source field

    Click qty in the S071_Rows source card. Desktop users can also drag a source field onto a grid column to insert before it.

  2. Find the new occurrence

    A second Qty column appears at the right. It has its own Show, Sort and Criteria controls. Scroll horizontally if needed.

  3. Choose a source, then set an alias

    In the new column’s Field dropdown choose UnitPrice. In the text box below it, press Enter/F2, type PriceCopy: [price], then Enter. The alias changes the output heading; the source remains price.

Back to contents

3. Select and deselect columns

Column selection is separate from cell focus and text selection. The “Selected N” status confirms structural selection.

  1. Select one column

    Click the ▾ selector above Qty in the top Column row. The column receives a visible selection border and its selector becomes pressed. Its accessible name identifies the column.

  2. Select a continuous range

    Hold Shift and click the ▾ selector above Enabled. Qty, UnitPrice and Enabled are now selected. Keyboard alternative: focus a cell, Ctrl+Space, then Shift+Left/Right.

  3. Select separate columns

    Press Escape to clear the range. Click Region’s ▾ selector, then hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) and click UnitPrice’s ▾ selector. Two separated columns are selected.

  4. Deselect all columns

    Click Cancel selection or press Escape. Selected 0 confirms that no columns are selected. Clicking a selected selector again also toggles it off; Ctrl/Cmd-click toggles individual additions.

Back to contents

4. Delete query columns, undo and redo

Deletion removes query design columns and their owned sort/criteria entries. It never deletes source records or source fields.

  1. Select the columns to remove

    Select Qty, then Shift-click UnitPrice. Click Delete selected, or press Delete while the grid selection has focus. A cell text editor keeps normal text-deletion behavior.

  2. Inspect the reduced design

    Only Region and Enabled remain. Click Undo to restore the removed columns and their query settings. A shared expression that still needs a removed operand can block deletion with an explanation.

  3. Restore the design

    Undo restores both columns in one operation. Redo removes them again. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work while navigating the grid; inside text editors they retain native text undo/redo.

Back to contents

5. Reorder and resize design columns

Design order controls output order and sort priority when you edit or move sort fields. Width is a temporary editing preference.

  1. Select a column and move it earlier

    Select UnitPrice, then click Move earlier. Move later moves the selection toward the right. These explicit controls also work on touch screens.

  2. Check the new order

    UnitPrice is now before Qty. You can also drag a desktop column by its dedicated handle. Dragging the resize divider changes width rather than order.

  3. Widen a column

    Drag the slim divider at the right of a column selector. Width stays between 140 and 600 pixels and does not change the query or result-table widths.

Back to contents

6. Show, hide and sort output fields

Unchecking Show hides an output field while preserving its criteria and sorting. Native result-table sorting is a separate presentation setting.

  1. Choose sorting and visibility

    In Qty’s Sort cell choose Descending. Uncheck Enabled’s Show checkbox. You can sort by several columns; design order determines their priority when edited.

  2. Filter by a hidden field

    Enter True under Enabled’s Criteria and click Apply query. The result contains 21 enabled source rows, ordered by Qty descending, without displaying Enabled.

Back to contents

7. Set criteria: AND and OR

Conditions in the same row use AND. Separate Or rows use OR within the same SQL stage. Repeat a condition on each alternative when it must apply to every alternative.

  1. Enter a criterion

    Focus the Qty Criteria cell and press Enter/F2. Type > 10, then press Enter to commit it. Clicking once only focuses a cell; Enter/F2 or double-click enters text editing.

  2. Add an AND condition

    On the same Criteria row, enter True under Enabled. This means qty > 10 AND enabled = True.

  3. Add an OR alternative

    Click Add OR row. In Or 1 enter < 5 under Qty and True under Enabled. The query means (qty > 10 AND enabled = True) OR (qty < 5 AND enabled = True). Remove Or 1 deletes that whole alternative.

  4. Check the expression and result count

    Apply query. This example matches 17 of 32 source rows. Expand Readable expression and query clauses to inspect parentheses and the corresponding WHERE clause.

Back to contents

8. Use the per-cell criterion builder

The … button in each Criteria cell opens a typed rule builder. It is an alternative to typing Access-style criterion text.

  1. Open a criterion’s rule editor

    Enter "North" under Region. Click the … button in that same Criteria cell. This edits only that cell’s condition; Edit whole expression edits the complete query filter.

  2. Choose an operator and value

    In the rule choose Region, starts with (case-insensitive), and N. The operator choices depend on the field type. Click Apply criterion, or Cancel to keep the old condition. Text comparisons in this Access-style query ignore case.

  3. Combine the rule with a numeric range

    Enter >= 10 And <= 20 under Qty on the same Criteria row, then Apply query. Five North rows match the range. The equivalent Region criterion is Like "N*". Clear criterion in the dialog removes its entire cell condition.

Back to contents

9. Add a condition for the whole criteria row

Edit row expression in the left gutter adds a condition alongside the individual field criteria on that row. This is useful for an expression that spans fields.

  1. Open the row-expression editor

    With Region = "North" and Qty > 10 on the Criteria row, click Edit row expression in the left gutter. Use + → insert rule to add a condition, or + → insert group for parentheses.

  2. Add a row-level rule and apply

    Choose Enabled, equals, false. Click Apply criterion, then Apply query. The row means region = "North" AND qty > 10 AND enabled = False, which matches 4 source rows. On a separate Or row the row expression belongs to that alternative only.

Back to contents

10. Build nested groups of criteria

Use Edit whole expression for parentheses and nested AND/OR groups. The visual builder applies the complete draft together; Cancel discards it.

  1. Open the whole-expression builder

    Start from Reset query and enter True under Enabled. Expand Readable expression and query clauses, then click Edit whole expression. The existing Enabled rule appears inside the root braces. Find the + insertion control after this rule.

  2. Insert a nested group

    Click the + after the Enabled rule to reveal two choices: insert rule and insert group (folder icon). Click Insert group at position 2 to add a parenthesized group beside the existing rule.

  3. Set AND outside, OR inside

    Use the + inside the new parentheses twice to insert two rules. Set the first to Qty / is greater than / 10 and the second to Qty / is less than / 5. Keep AND between Enabled and the group; choose OR between the two Qty rules. This means enabled = True AND (qty > 10 OR qty < 5).

  4. Apply and inspect the distributed criteria

    Click Apply expression in the dialog, then Apply query on the page. The equivalent grid repeats Enabled = True on each OR alternative. The result matches 17 source rows. Cancel in the dialog would discard the complete draft.

Back to contents

11. Zoom, clear a cell and recover from an invalid edit

Clear Cell changes a supported cell value; Delete Columns removes the entire query column. Invalid drafts keep the committed query and previous results intact.

  1. Edit a criterion in Zoom

    Focus the Qty Criteria cell and press Shift+F2, or open its cell context menu and choose Zoom. Type > 10 in the larger editor, then click Apply. Cancel or Escape keeps the previous value.

  2. Clear only the criterion

    Right-click the Qty Criteria cell, or focus it and press Shift+F10. Choose Clear Cell to remove its condition while keeping Qty in the design.

  3. Cancel an invalid draft

    Typing > without a value is invalid. The error explains the problem. Correct the draft and press Enter, or press Escape to discard it. Apply query cannot use an unfinished or invalid draft.

Back to contents

12. Create a calculated output column

Nonaggregate calculated columns support numeric source references, literals, parentheses and + − * /. This is a bounded local expression language.

  1. Type an alias and arithmetic expression

    Add another Qty occurrence. In its Field text box type LineTotal: [qty]*[price], then Enter. The alias appears as the result heading. Use the source name price, even though its caption is UnitPrice.

  2. Apply the calculated output

    Apply query to calculate LineTotal per source row. You can Show/hide and sort this output. Filter the source fields with Criteria; direct criteria on row-scalar output are disabled. Division by zero is reported as an execution error.

Back to contents

13. Add all fields with a wildcard

A wildcard is a real query column representing S071_Rows.*. It is different from selecting all current design columns.

  1. Add the source wildcard

    Click S071_Rows.* in the source card. A wildcard column appears at the right with its own Show control. Existing explicit columns remain, so adding the wildcard can intentionally produce repeated outputs.

  2. Expand before editing individual fields

    Select the wildcard column, then click Expand wildcard (it may be under the toolbar’s More button). This replaces it with separate field occurrences. Direct wildcard sorting is disabled; choose an explicit field instead.

  3. Use the expanded columns

    The wildcard becomes Region, Qty, UnitPrice and Enabled occurrences. Each can now be hidden, sorted, filtered or used with Totals. Existing compatible wildcard criteria are preserved during expansion.

Back to contents

14. Display grouped totals

Use Totals creates aggregate result rows. Group By fields form the grouping key; aggregate operations summarize records within each group.

  1. Enable the Total row

    Check Use Totals above the source card. All included columns initially use Group By. Keeping extra Group By fields can create many smaller groups.

  2. Choose grouping and aggregate functions

    Keep Region = Group By. Set Qty = Sum and UnitPrice = Avg. First uncheck Enabled’s Show box, then set its Total operation to Not used so it does not split groups. A shown field must have a Total operation. Numeric-only functions are disabled for nonnumeric fields.

  3. Read the grouped result

    Apply query. There are two result rows: North has SumOfqty 256 and AvgOfprice 3; South has SumOfqty 272 and AvgOfprice 4. The status distinguishes 32 matched source rows from 2 grouped result rows.

Back to contents

15. Filter before totals (WHERE) and after totals (HAVING)

WHERE filters source records before aggregation. HAVING filters the resulting groups. Their OR alternatives are independent; sharing a visual row does not merge the two SQL stages.

  1. Filter input records with Where

    Continue the totals query. Set Enabled’s Total operation to Where, then enter True in its Criteria. Where forces Show off. This filters the input records before Sum and Avg run.

  2. Filter groups with HAVING

    Enter > 170 under the Sum Qty column. Criteria beneath an aggregate or Group By field become HAVING. The condition means Sum(qty) > 170, rather than requiring each source qty to exceed 170.

  3. Check both stages

    Apply query. The enabled filter matches 21 source rows; HAVING leaves only South, with SumOfqty 192. North’s enabled-only sum is 160 and is excluded. Inspect the SQL view for separate WHERE and HAVING clauses.

Back to contents

16. Count records and choose other summaries

The same Total dropdown offers Count, Min, Max, First, Last, StDev and Var as well as Sum and Avg.

  1. Choose Max and Count

    Keep Region = Group By. Choose Max for Qty and Count for UnitPrice. Hide Enabled, then choose Not used for it. Count(field) counts non-null field values; Count(*) in a Total Expression counts every input row.

  2. Read the summary values

    Apply query. Each region has 16 non-null price values. North’s maximum Qty is 31; South’s is 32. Min/Max preserve the input type; StDev and Var use sample statistics and need at least two non-null numbers. First/Last follow source-row order within the group, before result sorting.

Back to contents

17. Create an aggregate expression

The Total Expression editor combines aggregate functions, group-key references, numbers and arithmetic. Remove row-scalar projections and expand wildcard columns before enabling Totals.

  1. Edit an aggregate formula

    Keep Region = Group By. For price and enabled first uncheck Show, then choose Not used. In Qty’s Total dropdown choose Expression. Enter Sum([qty]) / Count(*) in the dialog, then click Apply expression.

  2. Apply and reopen the formula

    The grouped output now contains average Qty computed by the formula: North 16 and South 17. Use Edit expression in the Total cell to reopen it. Cancel discards a dialog draft.

Back to contents

18. Edit grouping and ordering as ordered lists

The whole-expression dialog also offers GROUP BY, ORDER BY and All query clauses. These are useful when an ordering list is easier to inspect than the grid.

  1. Choose All query clauses

    In Expression clause select All query clauses. WHERE and HAVING use condition trees; GROUP BY and ORDER BY use ordered field lists. Scroll within the dialog to reach the lower lists. Apply expression commits all clause drafts together.

  2. Add an ordered sorting field

    Choose ORDER BY — ordered fields in Expression clause to focus just that list. Click Add field, choose [region], then DESC. Entries in this list are evaluated in order. GROUP BY has a similar field list without sort direction. Remove an entry with its Remove control; brace buttons can collapse each list independently.

  3. Apply all clause changes together

    Click Apply expression at the bottom of the dialog, then Apply query. South now precedes North because Region sorts descending. Cancel would discard all clause drafts together.

Back to contents

19. Inspect, edit and discard SQL drafts

The SQL editor uses the same local query model as the visual grid. It is not a database connection and does not execute arbitrary database commands.

  1. Read the generated SQL

    Expand SQL view and editor. The current query includes WHERE [qty] > 10. Editing SQL starts a draft; apply or discard that draft before other query changes.

  2. Apply the SQL draft

    Change > 10 to > 20 and click Apply SQL. This updates the visual criteria; click Apply query afterward to update results. Invalid SQL stays in the editor with an error.

  3. Discard unwanted SQL changes

    Discard SQL draft / load current query restores the committed SQL. Here the committed criterion remains > 20. Query results remain at the last successful Apply query.

Back to contents

20. Export and reload a query design

Export transfers the query definition into the page’s JSON text area. It does not automatically save a file or browser storage.

  1. Export the current definition

    Click Export query JSON, then scroll to Query JSON — export or reload. Copy the text into a file if you want to keep it. The definition includes fields, visibility, sorting, criteria and totals.

  2. Reload the exported definition

    After Reset query, click Reload query JSON to restore and apply the JSON already in the text area. A malformed or incompatible definition reports an error and leaves the previous result visible. Reopen S07.1 for its enhanced definitions.

Back to contents

21. Use touch selection and focused-column mode

On a narrow screen, pan the design grid horizontally to reach more columns. The row-name gutter stays visible. Commands may appear under the toolbar’s More button.

  1. Select separate columns on touch

    Tap Select columns to enter touch selection mode. Tap Region and UnitPrice selectors to toggle each one independently. Selected 2 confirms the selection. Cancel selection exits this mode.

  2. Show one full-width column

    Tap Focus column, using More if needed. The same grid cells now show one column beside the row labels. This is useful when the virtual keyboard leaves little space.

  3. Choose another focused field

    Use Focused column to switch to Qty, then edit its Criteria. Toggle Focus column again to return to the full grid. Use Apply query below the editor to refresh results.

Back to contents

Keyboard and criteria reference

These shortcuts belong to this browser editor. They do not claim exact behavior from a specific Microsoft Access version.

PurposeInteraction
Navigate cellsArrow keys; Home/End move to the first/last column. Tab leaves the grid entry.
Edit a text cellEnter or F2; double-click; typing starts editing. Enter commits; Escape cancels.
Validate and advance a text editTab. Invalid text stays focused until corrected or canceled.
Select a whole columnTop selector or Ctrl+Space from its cell. Shift+Left/Right extends selection.
Select several columnsShift-click a range; Ctrl/Cmd-click separate columns; touch Select columns mode.
Cancel selectionEscape or Cancel selection.
Column/cell commandsRight-click or Shift+F10. Arrow keys and Enter navigate a menu; Escape closes it.
Zoom textShift+F2 or the cell’s Zoom menu command.
Remove selected query columnsDelete while navigating the selected grid columns; text inputs keep native Delete/Backspace.
Undo / redo query operationsCtrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (Cmd on macOS), or toolbar Undo / Redo. Text inputs keep native text history.
Switch source/grid panesF6, scoped to this editor.

Criterion examples

Field type / purposeExample text
Number comparison> 10, <= 20, <> 5
Text equality"North"
BooleanTrue or False
Two bounds in one cell>= 10 And <= 20
Text alternatives"North" Or "South"
Null checkIs Null or Is Not Null
Field aliasPriceCopy: [price]
Numeric row calculationLineTotal: [qty]*[price]
Aggregate formula (Total Expression)Sum([qty]) / Count(*)

Use source names inside brackets: price is captioned UnitPrice. A blank criterion does not filter that field. Same-row conditions use AND; Or rows are alternatives. WHERE and HAVING are independent stages.

Troubleshooting and limits

  • Results have not changed: finish any text/dialog/SQL draft, then click Apply query. The page keeps the last successful results while you edit.
  • Too many grouped rows: extra Group By fields split groups. Set unwanted fields to Not used and uncheck Show, or use Where for input-only filtering.
  • Zero matching rows: check AND versus OR, quoted text, Boolean values, hidden-field criteria, and WHERE versus HAVING. A grouped query without matching inputs may have different aggregate behavior.
  • Delete or Apply is disabled: finish or cancel the current draft. Delete selected also requires a whole-column selection.
  • A command is missing: use the toolbar’s More button at narrow widths. Source and grid can also be collapsed under their section headings.
  • Deletion reports a dependency: a shared expression references a field you are removing. Edit/clear that expression first, or remove all dependent query columns together.
  • Wildcard or calculation blocks Totals: expand the wildcard and remove row-scalar calculated columns before enabling Totals. Use Total Expression for aggregate formulas.
  • Wildcard criteria: use a full source-field expression and keep referenced source fields as concrete occurrences in the query (hidden is allowed). Prefer explicit fields for per-column criteria.
  • A whole expression will not distribute into the grid: simplify it, Cancel, or use the explicit Apply as whole-table criterion option when offered. Inspect SQL to retain the exact grouping.
  • SQL-only HAVING: some aggregate formulas cannot map to simple grid cells. Use the whole-expression HAVING editor or SQL view; follow the displayed notice.
  • Scope: one synthetic source table; no joins, backend SQL execution, schema or record changes, device access, automatic saving, or arbitrary Access functions. Calculations support bounded numeric arithmetic. Direct criteria on row-scalar outputs are disabled; filter their source fields.
  • Two kinds of grouping: Total = Group By aggregates query results. Native result-table grouping is presentation only. This guide’s examples use query grouping.
  • Reset query: restores the initial design and applies it. The JSON text area stays available for an explicit Reload query JSON.
